Gumption

GUMP-shun · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Gumption is initiative, resourcefulness, and spirited courage; the willingness to take bold action.

It took real gumption for the new intern to speak up and correct the CEO's mistake in front of the whole board.

Worked Example

When the town's only bridge washed out, it was the teenagers' gumption -- not the officials' -- that got a temporary crossing built within a week.

Gumption is that mix of boldness and practical resourcefulness that gets things done when nobody else will act.

initiative

Antonyms

timidity

timidity: a lack of courage or confidence

passivity

passivity: a tendency to accept things without acting

How Strong Is It? — willingness → gumption → audacity

willingness vs. gumption

willingness vs. gumption: Willingness is a basic readiness to do something, without much boldness.

audacity vs. gumption

audacity vs. gumption: Audacity is bold, sometimes reckless daring -- even bolder than gumption.

Build the Word

The pieces

Put it together

Put it together: Gumption's exact origin is genuinely uncertain -- etymologists trace it to Scots dialect, possibly 'gaum' ('attention, common sense'), but no clean root is agreed on. Not every -tion word breaks apart neatly; this one is best learned whole.

Use the root in a new word: gaum

Use the root in a new word: gaum: Some word historians trace gumption to the old Scots dialect word 'gaum,' meaning attentiveness or common sense -- a nice fit, since gumption still implies having the sense to act boldly and the attention to know when.

Strength Check

Word Choice

Gumption is a warm, informal, almost old-fashioned word -- it praises someone's bold resourcefulness, and it works better in a story or conversation than in a formal report.
